title: India Have Bulletproof Workload Plan for New Zealand Tour, Morkel Says
excerpt: With the first Test starting four days after the ODI series ends, India will keep a cover group of bowlers in New Zealand — and Arshdeep Singh is in the conversation for a Test debut.
body:
• India bowling coach Morne Morkel says the team has a "bulletproof" workload plan for the New Zealand tour of five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests, covering every bowler including Jasprit Bumrah.
  • The first Test starts November 19 in Wellington, just four days after the ODI series ends, so a group of bowlers will stay behind in New Zealand as red-ball cover.
  • Left-arm pacer Arshdeep Singh — 100 T20Is played, two wickets short of 150 T20I wickets — is in the conversation for a Test debut, Morkel confirmed.
  • India A players including Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep are being prepared for red-ball cricket, and bowlers will be rotated through the ODI series for match practice.

India have a "bulletproof" plan to get their fast bowlers through a crowded tour of New Zealand, bowling coach Morne Morkel said on the eve of the third T20I, with left-arm pacer Arshdeep Singh also in contention for a Test debut. The tour packs five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests into a single trip, and the tightest squeeze comes at the end: the first Test begins on November 19 in Wellington, four days after the 50-over series finishes.

"Touch wood, it's a bulletproof plan at this point in terms of how we've got everything mapped out, but unfortunately not everything goes to plan."

— Morne Morkel, India bowling coach

How the plan works

Morkel said the tour was mapped out well in advance and every bowler is clear about his expected workload and role across formats. Three mechanisms carry the load. First, rotation in the ODI series, which starts November 4, will be used deliberately to give bowlers the game time they need before the Tests rather than simply resting them. Second, a group of bowlers will stay behind in New Zealand as cover for the two Tests in Wellington and Christchurch, with the final make-up of the unit to be decided once the team reads local conditions at that time of year. Third, the India A squad is being used as a red-ball preparation lane.

"The back-up that we have, the combinations are all in place in terms of the rotation, and they ensure that we prepare for the red-ball Tests and the 50-over series. Everyone is ready, including Bumrah," Morkel said, according to ANI's report carried by New Kerala and CricTracker's account of the press conference.

Arshdeep in the Test conversation

The most concrete selection news was about Arshdeep Singh. The 25-year-old completed his 100th T20I in the second match at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, taking two wickets, and sits two wickets short of becoming the first Indian bowler to reach 150 T20I wickets. He has 30 wickets in 18 ODIs, including a five-wicket haul, but has never played a Test.

His domestic red-ball record is the basis of the case: 73 wickets in 24 first-class matches at an average of 30.71, with two five-wicket hauls and best figures of 6 for 40. "On paper and in the back of our minds, there is a nice group of bowlers that can suit all conditions, and Arshdeep is definitely in that conversation. He's a guy that always works hard and ticks all the boxes, so if needed with the red ball, I'm pretty sure he'll be fine," Morkel said. Among the T20I squad's pacers, Arshdeep is also the only one named in the ODI squad, which keeps him match-ready across the tour's middle leg.

The A-team bridge

Pace bowlers Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep, both in the Test squad, are with the India A side for its three-match series, building red-ball overs before November 19. Test batters including captain Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel are also using the A games for time in the middle.

Morkel's caveat was built into the headline claim itself: plans hold until injuries or form intervene. What India have bought themselves with the structure — a cover group in-country, A-team preparation and planned ODI rotation — is options. Whether Arshdeep's name moves from conversation to cap will be decided closer to Wellington, once conditions, workloads and the ODI series have had their say.
